chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan, from al-Is, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the cheetahs and birds of prey, when trade is sought in them, and he said, 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy and sell cheetahs and birds of prey in Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the permissibility (*ibahah*) of trading in cheetahs and birds of prey, classifying them as valid commercial commodities (*mal*) despite their wild nature. This ruling reflects the early juristic consensus that utility and ownership determine marketability, distinguishing these animals from those explicitly prohibited for consumption or specific ritual uses. It highlights the flexibility of Shia commercial law in accommodating pre-Islamic and contemporary economic practices involving valuable livestock.
